Here the limits of the numerator and denominator are ${lim}_{x\to {\frac{\pi }{2}}^{-}}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)=-\infty $ and ${lim}_{x\to {\frac{\pi }{2}}^{-}}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)=\infty ,$ respectively, so we have the case $\frac{-\infty }{\infty }.$

Applying L'Hopital's rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {\frac{\pi }{2}}^{-}}\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)} & ={lim}_{x\to {\frac{\pi }{2}}^{-}}\frac{[\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)]^{′}}{{[\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)]}^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {\frac{\pi }{2}}^{-}}\frac{(-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x})}{(\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x})} \\  & =-{lim}_{x\to {\frac{\pi }{2}}^{-}}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x}{{sec}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x} \\  & =-{lim}_{x\to {\frac{\pi }{2}}^{-}}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x})}{(\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x})\operatorname{cos}⁡x} \\  & =-{lim}_{x\to {\frac{\pi }{2}}^{-}}\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡x}{(\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}){cos}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =-{lim}_{x\to {\frac{\pi }{2}}^{-}}{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =-{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
